public_rationale: Ramp's October 14, 2026 report restates that 1% of firms accounted for 80% of observed spending on OpenAI and Anthropic, without specifying the concentration statistic's underlying period [e1]. This measures concentration within Ramp's sample, not either provider's dependence on venture-financed token purchases during July–September 2026 [e1]. It therefore neither establishes nor refutes the claimed dependence [e1].
limitations: The sample does not identify how much of either provider's total revenue came from AI startups [e1].
The evidence does not match startup token purchases to customer receipts and financing flows [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic's and OpenAI's revenues are held up by venture capital by proxy via AI startups.

statement.excerpt: It doesn’t really matter what big businesses are or are not using Claude or ChatGPT — the underlying revenues of these companies are held up by venture capital by proxy.

from_speaker: what big businesses are or are not using Claude or ChatGPT
the underlying revenues of these companies
held up by venture capital by proxy
our_interpretation: The plain reading is substantial dependence by both providers on startup customers whose token purchases require continuing venture financing.
Held up means dependence material to maintaining revenue, not merely that some customers have venture investors.
The latest completed quarter before publication, July through September 2026, is the evaluation window for the current causal relationship; this is an evaluator choice.
The context relies on reported figures and sampled spending estimates, so the accounting basis is estimate.
criteria.support_condition: Representative customer revenue and funding records show that both providers materially depend on startup token purchases financed by venture capital rather than the startups' own customer receipts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that venture-financed startup purchases are immaterial to maintaining either provider's revenue, or that the relevant startup purchases are substantially self-funded from customer receipts.
